comment: D3 Round 25 — Megolm-equivalent ratcheting vectors. Spec authority: crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md (group-key ratcheting + per-message advance). The Megolm-equivalent in Arkret is a forward-secret group session keyed off the active MLS epoch: each sender owns a chain (chain_id, current_index, current_key) and at each message MUST advance the index by 1 (HKDF(current_key, salt='ck.megolm.ratchet.v1') => next_key). Recipients hold the (chain_id, [start_index, end_index]) key-window and may decrypt any message within. Pre-shared session keys distribute the (start_index, key_at_start) seed; old messages remain decryptable by holders of older indices, but rotating to a new chain MUST drop access to keys before the rotation point (forward secrecy bound: the post-rotation chain MUST NOT be derivable from any pre-rotation key).

encoder.rotation_trigger: MLS commit on ck.component.mls.epoch.v1 OR explicit ck.megolm.rotate

vectors.name: preshared_session_key_seeds_chain_at_index_zero
vectors.comment: Sender alice creates a fresh chain seeded at index=0 with a pre-shared session key (32 bytes). She shares (chain_id, 0, key_at_zero) to recipients via ck.device_message.megolm_session_share.v1. Recipient decrypt-window: [0, ∞).

expected.rationale: Pre-shared session key at index 0 lets recipients decrypt every message from the start of the chain forward.

vectors.name: per_message_ratchet_advance_one_step
vectors.comment: Sender sends message at index=5; before sending, she derives key_5 = HKDF(key_4, 'ck.megolm.ratchet.v1'). Recipient at decrypt-window [0, ∞) computes the same chain step and decrypts. Invariant: each send MUST advance the index by exactly 1; gaps require the sender to share the missed indices' keys via session-share.

expected.rationale: Each message advances the chain index by exactly 1; key_n+1 = HKDF(key_n, info='ck.megolm.ratchet.v1').

vectors.name: decrypt_old_message_with_archived_key
vectors.comment: Recipient bob received the session-share at index=10 with key_at_10. He now sees an OLD message at index=7 (sent before he joined). To decrypt, the sender MUST have included an out-of-band key-share at index=7. If sender included (7, key_at_7), bob can derive forward to verify, but cannot derive backward from key_at_10 (forward-secret).

expected.rationale: Forward-only KDF chain means a recipient given key_at_index=N can decrypt messages at indices >=N from THAT key alone; older messages require explicit out-of-band sharing.

vectors.name: rotation_drops_pre_rotation_access
vectors.comment: MLS epoch advances from 7 → 8 (membership change), triggering megolm rotation. Sender starts a NEW chain (chain_id_new) seeded at index=0 with a fresh random key. The new chain MUST NOT be derivable from the old chain (independent random seed + epoch_id binding). New members have access to chain_id_new from index=0; old members who left at the rotation point have access only to chain_id_old up to its terminal index.

expected.rationale: Rotation seeds a fresh chain bound to epoch_id_new; old chain ends at the rotation point so leavers cannot follow.

vectors.name: forward_secrecy_bound_pre_seed_undecryptable
vectors.comment: Recipient dave first received key share at index=20 (post-join). Even with full knowledge of the chain seed share at index=20, dave MUST NOT be able to compute key_at_index=15 (a message from before his share). Forward-secret KDF is one-way.

expected.rationale: Holder of key_at_index=N cannot derive any key_at_index<N (HKDF chain is one-way); message at earlier index is unrecoverable without out-of-band share.

negative_vectors.name: non_monotonic_index_rejected
negative_vectors.comment: Sender claims to be at index=8 but her recorded prior_index=10. Receiver MUST reject (replay or fork attempt).

expected.rationale: Within a chain the index MUST strictly increase per send; lower or equal index is a replay/fork.

negative_vectors.name: rotation_without_new_chain_id_rejected
negative_vectors.comment: Sender claims an MLS epoch rotation but reuses the old chain_id (effectively making the new chain derivable from the old). Forward-secrecy violation; receiver MUST reject.

expected.rationale: Rotation MUST mint a new chain_id with an independent random seed; reusing the old chain_id breaks the forward-secrecy bound.
